after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: Given the Contentstack client is mocked to return draft entry data, when a Content Author opens Live Preview for a draft entry in the CMS, the preview renders the draft content rather than the previously published version of that entry.

When a page is loaded without Live Preview parameters (standard published-content request), the website renders published content identically to its current behavior — no visual or functional regression in existing content display.
Given the Contentstack client is mocked to return draft entries for each brand, Live Preview renders draft content correctly on GO Transit, UP Express, and Metrolinx (MX) page types.
Protected pages that require authentication display the standard authentication or unauthorized prompt during Live Preview, rather than rendering the draft protected content.

Given the Contentstack client is mocked and signals an entry update, when a Content Author modifies a draft entry in the CMS, the Live Preview updates to reflect the change without requiring a manual full-page refresh.

notes: Novel story — Live Preview capability does not exist in the codebase. The Contentstack Stack initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts is the single attachment point: all 4 factory methods and 20+ callers flow through it. Currently only delivery_token is configured for published content. The vendor docs prescribe live_preview config + ContentstackLivePreview.init() + onEntryChange for CSR (Pages Router, not App Router). Acceptance criteria are empty; VCs derived from description alone.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with useful context about the codebase. I reviewed the actual source files: (1) src/services/contentstack.ts confirms the Stack is initialized with only delivery_token, no live_preview config; (2) the app uses Pages Router (src/pages/ directory with _app.tsx, [[...slug]].tsx); (3) no live preview code exists anywhere (confirmed via search). All 15 ACs are new. Key design decisions reflected: AC-2/13 enforce security boundary (draft must not leak); AC-3 addresses the env-validation pattern already in contentstack.ts (missing vars currently throw — preview vars must not crash the app); AC-6 addresses the story's stated limitation about protected pages; AC-7/11 cover error/resilience paths; AC-12 addresses JSON RTE rendering which is explicitly handled in the current code via Utils.jsonToHTML; AC-15 reflects the Pages Router constraint noted in openspec's notes (vendor docs prescribe CSR onEntryChange for Pages Router, not App Router).
